sections.h2: Where is the Hillsdale County Register of Deeds and how do I submit a document?
sections.html:
The office is in the Hillsdale County Office Building at 33 McCollum St., Room 212, Hillsdale, Michigan 49242, and the number is (517) 437-2231. Hours are Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Electronic documents may be sent at any time, though they are accepted and processed only during posted hours and not on holidays.

The county takes e-recording through four vendors: Indecomm, ePn, Simplifile and CSC/Ingeo. Payment is by ACH under the vendor agreements, vendors may add their own fees, and recorded documents come back to the submitter electronically. The register reserves the right to reject an electronic submission that breaks the Michigan Recording Act.

For paper filings, personal checks are not accepted. Certified funds such as cashier's checks and money orders are. The page also lists three local title companies in the city of Hillsdale for anyone who wants help preparing the deed, since the office does not draft documents, supply templates or give advice that could pass for legal advice.

sections.h2: What are the recording fees in Hillsdale County?
sections.html:
Recording costs $30.00 per document, covering every page, under MCL 600.2567 as amended by PA 224 of 2016. The county's fee page lists the following charges.

Hillsdale County statutory deed fees (Register of Deeds)
ItemAmount
Recording, all pages$30.00
Each added assignment or discharge$3.00
Tax certificate, up to 5 descriptions$5.00
Grantor or grantee search$5.00 minimum, 50 cents per year searched
Real estate record copy$1.00 per page
Certification of a copy$5.00 per document

State and federal tax lien searches run $3.00 per name, and plats are $2.00 per page to copy. A transfer tax calculator sits on the register's page for quick estimates, and county staff will confirm the final figure when the deed is presented.

sections.h2: How much transfer tax is due on a Hillsdale County sale?
sections.html:
Transfer tax is charged on the value of the land, stepped up to the next $500. Under MCL 207.504 the county charges 55 cents per step, and under MCL 207.525 the state charges $3.75, so a Hillsdale County sale pays $4.30 per $500 of value.

At a $175,000 price there are 350 steps. State tax comes to $1,312.50, county tax to $192.50, and the total to $1,505.00. At the county's median owner-occupied value of $176,100 the value rounds to $176,500, which makes 353 steps and $1,517.90.

  • The full value must appear on the deed, or a value affidavit must be attached.
  • Any exemption claimed must be written on the instrument itself.
  • County exemptions are in MCL 207.505 and state exemptions in MCL 207.526.
  • A land contract is exempt while legal title stays with the seller, and a deed in fulfillment must reference the contract.

sections.h2: What did the 2018 recording law changes require in Hillsdale County?
sections.html:
The Hillsdale register sent title companies, attorneys and lenders a notice on the bills signed June 20, 2018 (Public Acts 191 to 200). The changes that affect most deeds took effect 90 days later, on September 19, 2018, and they still shape what the office will accept.

  • A document conveying an interest as a survivor needs a certified death certificate or other proof of death recorded by liber and page, or filed with the deed as its own recorded document. Stapling a copy to the deed no longer works (MCL 565.48).
  • A document from outside Michigan must meet Michigan recording requirements, except page formatting (MCL 565.203).
  • Any instrument with text in a language other than English needs an English translation attached (MCL 565.201).

The office also stresses that court orders must be certified and sealed by the clerk, that dates cannot be missing from a notary acknowledgment, and that tax certificates and fees are due when the document is presented.

sections.h2: Who certifies taxes and what happens to unpaid taxes in Hillsdale County?
sections.html:
The County Treasurer issues the tax certificate that a warranty deed, a land contract, or an assignment of a land contract with a warranty clause needs under MCL 211.135. The Treasurer's number is (517) 437-4700, and the certificate costs $5.00 for up to five descriptions.

The Treasurer's yearly delinquent tax notice walks owners through the last stage of the foreclosure law. It sets a date after which a name will appear in a newspaper advertisement that runs two consecutive weeks before the Show Cause Hearing in Circuit Court. A little later the office stops accepting partial payments and personal or business checks, and from then on takes only cash, cashier's checks, money orders and credit cards with a 3% convenience fee. The Treasurer warns owners that losing a valuable property over unpaid tax is avoidable.

For a seller with an old tax balance, ask the Treasurer for a payoff figure before listing, because the deed cannot be recorded without the certificate.

sections.h2: What should a seller know about Hillsdale County?
sections.html:
Hillsdale County was described by the Territorial legislature in 1829 and organized in 1835. It is named for its rolling terrain. Hillsdale is both the seat and the largest city, and Hillsdale College is based there. The county covers 607 square miles, is the only Michigan county with a border on both Indiana and Ohio, and holds the southernmost point in Michigan. The headwaters of two different St. Joseph Rivers rise inside its lines.

Winters are cold and summers warm: the average July high is 82 degrees and the January high is 29 degrees, with June the wettest month at about 4.3 inches.

The Census Bureau's 2025 estimate is 45,738 residents, close to the 45,746 counted in 2020 and below the 46,688 of 2010. For 2020 to 2024 it reports 17,860 households, a median owner-occupied home value of $176,100, an owner-occupied rate of 82.0%, median household income of $64,242, median gross rent of $832, and 23.2% of residents aged 65 or older. A county where more than four in five housing units are owner-occupied has relatively few rentals, so most deeds recorded here come from owners selling a home they lived in.

The register also runs a free Property Alert service that warns landowners of possible property fraud, which is worth signing up for before or after a sale.

faqs.q: How much does Hillsdale County charge to record a deed?
faqs.a: $30.00 per document, covering all pages, plus transfer tax on a sale and a $5.00 tax certificate for a warranty deed.

faqs.q: Does Hillsdale County accept electronic recording?
faqs.a: Yes. The county accepts e-recording through Indecomm, ePn, Simplifile and CSC/Ingeo, with payment by ACH, and vendors may charge additional fees.

faqs.q: Can I pay the Hillsdale County register with a personal check?
faqs.a: No. Personal checks are not accepted. Certified funds such as a cashier's check or money order are.

faqs.q: What are the Hillsdale County Register of Deeds hours?
faqs.a: Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., at 33 McCollum St., Room 212. Electronic documents can be sent anytime but are processed during posted hours.

faqs.q: What is the transfer tax on a $175,000 sale in Hillsdale County?
faqs.a: $1,505.00, made up of $1,312.50 state tax and $192.50 county tax, based on 350 steps of $500 at $4.30 per step.
